source.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
source.authors: Yamini Bansal; Preetum Nakkiran; B. Barak

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests representation compatibility using model stitching, a different operational measure from representational distance metrics such as CKA.
record.gate_note: Rows below record the study's stitching and CKA outcomes, including results stated in text whose plotted values are not given numerically. The reported 75% ± 1 and 68.8% accuracies characterize the ImageNet model performance, not stitching outcomes, so they are not separate rows. The freeze-training accuracy result and values used to select layers are not rows because they do not themselves measure representation alignment.
record.test_reason: Uses low-capacity linear (1x1 conv) model stitching, with CKA as a comparison, on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet vision models. It tests whether models differing in seed, training samples, objective, labels, width or training time have interchangeable representations. This bears directly on V3, V4, V6 and V7. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. The authors conclude that model stitching shows good networks of the same architecture learn similar representations, even across seeds, samples and supervised vs self-supervised training (stitching connectivity of SGD). Early layers are robust to label changes while later layers depend on training details, and more data, width or training time give better, compatible representations. They argue stitching reveals what CKA cannot. They do not say conclusions depend on the stitching method (kernel size has minimal effect); they note that stitching depends on the downstream task and that cross-architecture stitching is tricky.
record.recipe_differences: Revisits and extends Lenc and Vedaldi's model-stitching approach. Uses task-trained, low-capacity stitchers—typically 1×1 convolutions with batch normalization for convolutional models—and reports downstream task loss or error; it also compares outcomes with CKA.
record.method_sensitivity: Compatibility and measured similarity depend on layer, training condition, and measure: the study reports layer-dependent effects, asymmetric width comparisons, and different conclusions from CKA versus stitching. Stitcher kernel sizes 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 have minimal impact in the tested CIFAR-10 comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Representations from models with more data, width or training time can be plugged into weaker models and improve their performance. The relation is asymmetric: it does not hold from narrow into wide.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Better-resourced models learn improved versions of the same representations, ordered and compatible with weaker models' representations (asymmetric 'more is better').

fits_no_version.finding: Early layers of trained networks stitch to untrained random networks with low penalty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-layer similarity across models partly reflects architecture or random features rather than learned convergence.

record.problems: Most per-layer stitching outcomes are shown only in figures without exact values. The experiments are in vision; the authors note that cross-architecture stitching requires careful choice of stitcher. The claim's broad cross-modal scope is not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible alignment result was omitted. Appendix B.4's freeze-training performance result is not included because it evaluates a training scheme rather than measuring representation alignment; layer-selection values are also excluded under the gate rules.

untested.parts: No measurement of alignment rising with model size or capability across different architectures, objectives or data. The 'more is better' results show plug-in improvement, not convergence with scale.
Does not test individual units or bases versus shared subspaces. Stitching shows only linear compatibility.
No cross-architecture stitching (the authors note it is tricky), no relative representations, no unpaired alignment. Vision only.
No interpretable feature or circuit matching.
No out-of-distribution inputs. No sweep of CKA settings or neighbour counts.
All compared pairs share the input distribution, so the study cannot separate shared data from a common model of reality. No plateau analysis.

missing.what: Table 1 summary values: CKA for different initializations 'varies (can be 0)' vs stitching up to 3% error; self-supervision stitching up to 5% error
CKA between two different-seed E2E networks, and the statement that SimCLR-vs-E2E CKA differs more than two random initializations
Fine-tuning instead of stitching fails to distinguish a trained from a random ResNet-164 bottom, overestimating similarity

record.verdict_notes: V1 links were removed. The 'more is better' experiments test plug-in improvement, not whether alignment increases with scale. r22 was changed from reversed to cannot_determine because the text only denies an improvement. r8-r11 carry an 'observed' state for V4, but the V7 effect (incompleteness) is absent there under stitching; a per-version state would be clearer. All results are in vision, with same-architecture pairs except the width experiments.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test broad scaling across architectures, objectives, data and modalities together, or measure similarity rising continuously with size and capability.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation comparison.
Tests compatibility by stitching, not whether the same individual features or shared subspaces are learned; does not assess individual units or bases.
Tests stitching with a trained, low-capacity layer, not relative representations, stitching layers, or alignment without paired data.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits.

Compares stitching and CKA and varies layers and some training settings; does not report an out-of-distribution input test or a systematic sweep of neighbour count or other similarity-measure settings.
Shows incomplete and layer-dependent compatibility, but does not establish that shared data or objectives cause alignment rather than a common model of reality.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Same-architecture CIFAR-10 models (ResNet-18 variants, ResNet-164, Myrtle-CNN, ViT) from different seeds or disjoint samples
labels.reason: Section 4 reports near-base error at every tested stitch point for the seed pairs and a similar result for disjoint samples (r1–r7). This establishes task-compatible representations after alignment.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Pairs differing in seed, objective (SSL vs supervised), training time, more data or greater width, via 1x1 conv stitching
labels.reason: Low-capacity stitching preserves or improves task performance in these conditions (r1–r11, r18–r21). CNN stitchers use 1×1 convolutions with batch normalization; the ViT row r6 instead uses a token-wise linear map.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Changed label distribution in later layers, fewer training samples in mid-layers, 100%-noise labels, early layers matched by a random network
labels.reason: Changed labels and reduced training samples produce depth-dependent compatibility, and 100%-noise training is excluded from early-layer equivalence (r12–r16). The random-network control r27 qualifies an inference of learned convergence, rather than showing failed interchangeability.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: CKA versus stitching for SSL-vs-supervised, width and sample-count comparisons
labels.reason: CKA and functional stitching give different conclusions for supervised–SimCLR, width and sample-count comparisons; the stated CKA values and low or negative stitching penalties are reported in Section 5 and Appendix B.2.3.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Training-time comparison and stitcher kernel-size settings
labels.reason: The tested V6 effect is absent in both listed conditions: CKA and stitching agree for 80 versus 160 epochs (r26), and kernels 1–9 have minimal impact (r29). These are null results for dependence in the specified conditions.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Models trained with coarse or noisy labels, later layers
labels.reason: Compatibility is limited to roughly the first half of the network under coarse or partially noisy labels, supporting incomplete convergence and dependence on training labels (r12–r14). The broader common-reality explanation is untested.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Same-architecture ImageNet and CIFAR-10 models trained with different objectives (SimCLR/SwAV/DINO vs supervised), stitching measure only
labels.reason: The models remain stitching-connected across tested layers; CIFAR-10 supervised–SimCLR penalties are at most 3% and within the seed-pair range (r8–r11). This challenges incompleteness under functional stitching, while shared input data and geometric incompleteness remain possible.

relation.reason: Reports direct experiments on compatibility across initializations, objectives, labels, sample counts, widths and training times, including comparisons with CKA.

tranche.reason: Uses task-trained model stitching as a functional comparison of independently trained representations, alongside CKA, to address representation convergence.

source_check.notes: ResNet stitching explicitly occurs between residual blocks; these results do not test inside-block interfaces or establish complete geometric alignment. Sample-count descriptions are inconsistent: Section 6 specifies a 10K top model, Appendix B.2.3 mentions a 5K receiver, and Appendix B.4 describes full-data comparisons.

statements.correction: Supervised–SimCLR CIFAR-10 ResNet-18: CKA 0.35–0.9; maximum stitching penalty 3%; stitching connectivity in both directions. Sample comparison: 5K versus 25K; CKA as low as 0; negative stitching penalty reported. Width comparison: 0.25× versus 2×; CKA as low as 0.7.
statements.problem: The supervised–SimCLR comparison is correct, but this study does not report a deliberately CKA-penalized self-stitch or CKA below 0.7 from that intervention; cited row r25 concerns training sample counts.

statements.correction: 80 versus 160 epochs: CKA and stitching both indicate similar representations. Stitcher kernels {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}: minimal effect on test error. V6 verdict for these tested conditions: challenges.
statements.problem: The stability results are correct, but this study's listed conditions show absent metric or setting dependence, rather than mixed dependence warranting limits_scope.
